$comment: A public proposal, bridged from the API queue. Do not edit this file to resolve the proposal: change the record it targets and fill in `resolution`.

target.name: Regenerate an entire epidermis from gene-corrected autologous stem cells

summary: Prademagene zamikeracel (VIITAL, NCT04227106) is a completed randomised Phase 3 of autologous COL7A1-corrected epidermal sheets that met both co-primary endpoints and was approved by the FDA in 2025 — the map has no record of it
rationale: 'Prademagene zamikeracel for recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa wounds (VIITAL): a two-centre, randomised... trial', The Lancet, 2025, doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(25)00778-0 (indexed in Europe PMC as a phase III randomised controlled trial). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04227106 is COMPLETED, Phase 3, sponsor Abeona Therapeutics, co-primary outcomes wound healing and pain reduction. The product is an autologous gene-corrected keratinocyte (epidermal stem cell) sheet, the same class as the Hirsch 2017 graft the map currently cites, but with randomised evidence and a regulatory approval behind it. Suggested edits: add the Lancet paper and the FDA approval as sources; add a claim at L5 (randomised, approved) supporting hrm:capability/epidermis-gene-corrected-stem-cell-replacement; reconsider that capability's rung, which is currently L4 on the basis of single-group case reports. Note that this is RDEB (COL7A1, dystrophic) whereas the existing records are JEB (LAMB3, junctional) — a reviewer should decide whether one capability covers both. Surfaced by ChatGPT (GPT-5.6, web search) during the 2026-09-14 prediction run; verified against Europe PMC and the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API by Claude Code. Abstract and registry metadata only; no figure-level reading.
